contentList.content: Light as moonbeams, these githyanki march boots remember the silver-grey hush of the Astral Plane. The leather still recoils when struck, as if expecting the wearer to step half a world away.
Spider silk, gold thread, and the dark perfume of fear. The robe was sewn for a man who would be a god of tyrants, and the cloth still leans toward any who would wear his crown.
Surrounds you with an <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="AURA_OF_TERROR">Aura of Terror</LSTag>.

'You poor sods couldn't grasp how effortless this magical hootie-wootie business is for me,' said the loudest sorcerer at the academy ball, the night before he vanished into a pocket dimension of his own making.
The fingertips are studded with shards of meteoric iron, ringed in faint violet fire. They were made for hunters who learn the weight of a heart from the way a blade slows passing through it.
Featherlaced and supple of sole, used to round up enemies and outrun friends. The cobbler swore the leather was treated with the breath of a wind elemental, but he also swore he was a prince.

Stitched in the workshops of the Circle of Eight. The wizard Otiluke favoured this weave, claiming it would deflect any spell aimed below the shoulder, including, he insisted, the bills of his tailor.
Worn by the wizard Tenser the day Mystra herself confirmed his place in the Circle of Eight. The threads remember every spell he ever cast, and shimmer faintly when great magic is near.
Surrounds you with a <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="FIRE_SHIELD_CHILL">Fire Shield: Chill</LSTag>.

The horns of this helm bore witness to the first murder between Bhaalspawn. Sarevok's last sight as a mortal was his sibling's knife, and the cult of Bhaal still considers no act more holy than that quiet, family business.
Fills you with the <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="ALCH_ELIXIR_BLOODLUST">Elixir of Bloodlust</LSTag>.
Forged from the ash of a paladin's funeral pyre, this plate keeps a slow ember burning in its rivets. Cold to the eye, warm to the wearer, and unforgiving to anything that strikes it.
Cloaks you in a <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="FIRE_SHIELD_WARM">Fire Shield: Warm</LSTag>.
Plain plate gloves, almost humble. They carry no glow, no sigil, only the cool certainty of every soldier who has ever worn them and won.
Optimistic in shape, suspicious in purpose. The brim leans forward as if eavesdropping, and the felt has been heard, on quiet nights, to mutter the answers to questions no one has yet asked.
Grants <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="FOXS_CUNNING">Fox's Cunning</LSTag> and <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="DETECT_THOUGHTS">Detect Thoughts</LSTag>.

Tenser wore this hood at his ordination. After the ceremony Otiluke and Bigby played their famous trick on him. What the trick was, no one ever learned, but those two pranksters spent the next month sneezing constellations.
Once the property of the royal house of Threskel. The gauntlets remember the prince's grip, and lend a measure of his legendary skill to any hand that fits.
A tabard of officer's issue covers this perfectly preserved harness. The plate was clearly worn into more parades than battles, yet it has not lost its measure of presence.
Grants <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="PROTECTION_FROM_EVIL_AND_GOOD">Protection from Evil and Good</LSTag> and <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="RIGHTEOUS_CLARITY">Righteous Clarity</LSTag>.
Druid silk dyed with crushed malachite. In stillness the cloth shows no pattern, in meditation a tracery of leaves appears across the cowl, and in storms the leaves move.
A reliquary of Tyr, struck for the chief justices of the Order of the Triad. The metal is cool to the touch, and lets out a slow protective light when the wearer stands beside an ally.
Surrounds you with an <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="AURA_OF_PROTECTION">Aura of Protection</LSTag>.
Worn by paladins who walked away from their oaths and learned to wear that loss as armour. The metal is cold even in summer, and warmer than it should be in winter.
Surrounds you with an <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="AURA_OF_HATE">Aura of Hate</LSTag>.
Forged from the silver of the Towers of Devotion, where the first oaths of paladinhood were sworn. Plain in shape, deep in resolve. Its weight is the weight of a kept promise.
Surrounds you with an <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="AURA_OF_DEVOTION">Aura of Devotion</LSTag> and grants <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="DIVINE_FAVOR">Divine Favour</LSTag>.
A small kindness in metal. The hand that wears it gestures more easily, and listeners lean a little closer than they meant to.
Tiny shields, targes, bucklers, and bracers are pressed faintly into the band, an entire armoury's lineage worn on a single finger.

Once worn by Edith Cluckle, who at six years of age asked the great Otiluke to take her as an apprentice. He laughed. Mystra did not, and gave the girl this robe instead. Edith outlived Otiluke by sixty years.
Grants <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="MAGE_ARMOR">Mage Armour</LSTag> and <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="BLADE_WARD">Blade Ward</LSTag>.

Hammered for the first of the Bhaalspawn to dream of godhood. The plate drips with that ambition still, and almost every historian agrees that Sarevok had a face built for a helm: too much chin, and far too many teeth.
Marks you with <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="END_ALLYABILITIES_BHAALBUFF">A Most Bloody Inheritance</LSTag>.
Soft soles cushion the ankle, fine bronze springs sewn into the heel. Worn by the Dawnrunners of Silverymoon, who race the sun along the city walls each summer dawn.

A circlet of woven feathers and oak leaf, kept green by the wearer's breath. Druids of the Owl-Watcher claim that any beast within earshot will speak to it, although most beasts have nothing they wish to say.
Grants <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="OWLS_WISDOM">Owl's Wisdom</LSTag> and <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="PETPAL">Speak with Animals</LSTag>.
